title: Return-home smell and sound inspection
summary: A safe-edge inspection before entering a home after flood, fire, earthquake, storm, gas concern, or long absence. It uses smell, sound, water, heat, and animals as warning signals.
content: It uses smell, sound, water, heat, and animals as warning signals. Core sequence: 1) Pause at the safest outside edge and listen for hissing, sparking, running water, cracking, or animal movement. 2) Smell for gas, smoke, sewage, chemicals, mold, or spoiled food before touching switches or doors. 3) Look for sagging ceilings, shifted walls, standing water, broken glass, or insects before stepping in. 4) Leave immediately and call the right authority if smell, sound, structure, water, or electricity suggests hidden danger.
materials: camera or notebook for visible observations
closed shoes and gloves ready but not yet used inside
contact numbers for utilities and building owner
